title: Guillermo Rauch's 2016 in review: ZEIT, Now, Next.js, Hyper and the ideas shaping his thinking
summary: Rauch recaps his first year building ZEIT: Now (immutable one-command deploys), World (free DNS), Hyper (an extensible terminal) and Next.js. He explains the product philosophy behind each, plus ideas on accessibility, universal code style and being wrong about reactions.

principles.text: Make deployment a single command and let every deploy be immutable with its own URL, so dev, staging and production are one system.
principles.quote: One is that the same system gives you development, staging and production all in one. You can deploy to build, test and iterate during development. You can _stage_ by simply sharing these links to your co-workers or clients, before you make them live.

principles.text: Remove dependencies on a specific person or team for infrastructure chores like DNS and SSL; they kill productivity and become invisible barriers.
principles.quote: Processes like that kill productivity and create invisible barriers for product engineers. Worse yet, after a while you just get used to it.

principles.text: Build for composable, focused tools: CLIs resist bloat because they do one thing well, compose, and are easy to replace; text is fast and searchable.
principles.quote: Most CLI programs adhere to the [Unix Philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_philosophy). Unlike most apps and websites, it's hard for these programs to bloat. They tend to do one thing well. They compose. They are easy to replace.

principles.text: Bring back good old ideas (zero setup, filesystem routing, pre-rendered HTML) and generalize across paradigms rather than choosing between site and app.
principles.quote: Websites tend to _pre-render markup_ and download code _lazily_. Apps tend to download _everything_ in advance, and therefore tend to feel faster afterwards. Now we're showing you can do both.

principles.text: Make errors actionable by attaching a URL to every error message, pointing users to a resource you can update over time instead of making them Google it.
principles.quote: Instead of having our users Google error messages or codes, we can point them to a resource we can update over time and others can comment on!

principles.text: Hedge the risk of a startup by founding it with people you love and respect; adopt universal code style tools to stop wasting time debating style.
principles.quote: If there's a way to [hedge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedge_(finance)) the risky personal investment of launching a startup company, it surely must be to do it with people you love and respect.
